items: A redesigned Studio with a large OBS preview and webcam controls alongside it.
Separate Voice, Connections and Activity workspaces.
Save an encrypted OBS preset and reconnect automatically at startup.
Load voice API keys from your local .env file.
Exact webcam placement, size, undo and restore commands skip the second cloud interpretation request.
Rebuild and restart SceneSense from the app header.
See whether the restart installed local changes or the app was already up to date.
See a What’s new list after an update, showing changes added since the previous build.
Restart status now appears in a pixelated comic bubble anchored to the restart button.
Typewriter text includes release notes, with Show all, Close and reduced-motion support.
Update bubbles now have a thin border, rounded corners and a smooth pointer instead of pixelated edges.
Save multiple OBS presets with names and switch between them from a dropdown.
Rename a preset without reentering its encrypted password, and choose one preset for startup reconnect.
Existing saved connections are preserved as My OBS studio.
Ctrl+Shift+Z now explains missing setup and has a keyboard fallback while SceneSense is focused.
Every voice action now uses OpenAI Decisions, including placement, size, undo and restore.
Improved handling of partial speech avoids repeatedly cancelling valid requests.
See voice feedback in Studio, plus keyboard, audio, transcription and action diagnostics in Voice.
A floating voice notch with the Libraries.dev orb appears above other apps while you speak.
The notch shows connecting, listening, finishing and brief success or error states without stealing focus or mouse clicks.
The Voice screen now uses the same animated orb indicator.
Check a game frame for important information hidden by the webcam, with an evidence image and suggested placement.
Optional watching can suggest changes or move after two matching checks; voice and manual controls take priority.
Image checks use cropped game regions, reject stale layouts and stop when sources change.
Sense now uses the animated 32px Libraries.dev Mech avatar, with a working state during scene analysis.
The transcription display now uses the Mobile voice glow, reacting to held speech and sweeping while the command finishes.
Sense now points at possible obstructions in the OBS preview, explains suggestions and previews camera moves using the 32px Mech avatar.
Apply, keep the current position, or undo Sense’s last move. Expired and changed layouts are rejected.
Shorter interface copy throughout, with voice timings and longer explanations tucked into expandable details.
Control watching, scene checks, Sense suggestions, app navigation, previews and setup actions through dictation. Saying Sense is optional.
Select saved presets, sources and microphones by their displayed names. Find the full list under Voice commands.
App actions wait for final speech after key release; webcam placement remains responsive during speech. Fresh Sense suggestions survive voice handoff.
A slightly larger desktop voice notch now shows the animated 32px Sense Mech while listening. Finishing and applied states retain their orb animations.
A dark theme with a saved light/dark switch, including Sense bubbles, forms and voice effects.
The disconnected OBS preview uses a static placeholder; the image-loading animation was removed after a reported freeze.
Switch themes by voice with dark theme, light theme, or toggle theme.
Removed the disconnected-preview animation and its graphics initialization after a reported app freeze.
Dark mode and all existing OBS and voice controls remain available.
Hands-free voice executes complete commands after a short speech pause and keeps listening for the next instruction.
Use Annotate to select an app element, save a change request locally, and export feedback for Codex.
Copy annotation feedback as JSON directly to your clipboard, or download it as before.
Dark mode now uses an accessible sliding toggle switch in the header.
Annotation copying now uses the native desktop clipboard.
The theme switch label follows the active light or dark mode.
Sense distinguishes uncertain detection from a detected obstruction with no clear destination.
Expand decision details to inspect current obstruction and candidate-corner scores.
Game analysis explicitly recognizes selectable event cards and partial menu overlap.
Sense searches eight edge positions at current, 75% and 60% size, with a minimum size for smaller candidates.
Preview the exact suggested position and size before approving new placements.
Position and size transitions animate together in OBS, with external-change detection and exact undo.
Possible obstructions can offer a placement preview at 70% confidence.
Automatic movement still requires 90% obstruction confidence; lower-confidence suggestions require approval.
Game analysis uses a sharper 1280px snapshot and explicitly checks partial overlap with text, icons and controls.
Suggestion confidence starts at 70%; automatic movement retains its 90% threshold.
Sense now searches only the four corners at supported sizes and ranks qualifying placements by the lowest obstruction score.
If no corner is sufficiently clear, the webcam stays unchanged.
Sense prioritizes clear corner placements, then searches a 5 × 5 canvas grid at supported webcam sizes.
Interior placements require preview approval; fallback image requests run in bounded batches.
Sense appears twice as large in the preview suggestion overlay.
Voice microphone prepares automatically at startup once API configuration is loaded.
The selected microphone is remembered, with an option to disable automatic preparation. Audio uploads only during voice dictation.
Sense welcomes you from the desktop notch with a time-aware comic bubble and a playful greeting.
Greetings dismiss after eight seconds and yield immediately to voice dictation.
Sense’s startup comic bubble matches the saved app theme and updates when you switch between dark and light mode.
Clear Corner is now SceneSense’s logo in the header, favicon and desktop window icon.
Light mode uses the white Clear Corner mark on its purple rounded-square tile.
Voice now includes a searchable guide with example commands for all registered Sense capabilities and webcam controls.
Startup bubbles include playful meme-inspired lines; the time-of-day greeting still follows local time.
The desktop notch now uses the same sound-reactive Voice glow as the transcription panel, driven by the existing microphone meter.
Finishing retains its orb and adds the processing beam; greeting bubbles stay quiet.
Enable Conversational Sense on the Voice page for natural text replies in the notch and app.
The remembered toggle can disable chat replies without disabling commands or startup greetings.
Replies use OpenAI text generation, with session-only conversation context and no tool access.
Ask Sense for gaming, Twitch and industry news using live web search through your existing OpenAI key.
News briefings include clickable source citations, requested dates and a checked timestamp on the Voice page.
Gaming headlines, Twitch updates and industry news shortcuts are available beside conversational controls.
The notch stays visible with searching or thinking feedback while Sense works.
Long answers show a short summary in the comic bubble, with an Open Voice button for the complete result and sources.
Clear Corner opens with the installed ReactDrops Liquid Glass Logo entrance, ending on the original mark alone against black.
Reduced motion and unsupported graphics use a static logo; a separate-window timeout protects access to the app.
Sense’s greeting follows the startup sequence.
The launch animation and fallback use white in light mode and black in dark mode, matching your saved app theme.
Connect your studio in the disconnected preview now uses the ReactDrops Chromatic Button with spectrum reflections, spotlight hover and blur-up entrance.
Animated Topographic Flow behind the app tiles, with light and dark colors, pointer interaction, and reduced-motion support.
First-time visitors can take a Sense-guided, point-and-explain tour of Studio, Connections, Voice, watching, Activity, theme and updates.
Skip, go back or replay the tour anytime using Tour. Tour pointers never run app commands.
Sense now uses Showcase Pointer for webcam obstruction explanations and proposed placements, matching the guided tour.
The pointer indicates the blocked area, then moves to the suggested placement during preview. Pointing never triggers OBS actions.
Topographic Flow keeps its ambient animation without reacting to the cursor.
Remove your webcam background locally through the OBS Background Removal plugin, or switch back to Original in Studio.
Say ‘Remove my webcam background’ or ‘Restore my webcam background’. Webcam position and size stay unchanged.
Plugin checks and setup guidance explain missing installations and avoid changing other background-removal filters.
